hook: RBI draft: a *trusted person* could approve your big transfers
hook_b: RBI draft: a *trusted person* could approve your big transfers
tldr: RBI's draft rules let customers name a trusted person to approve large transfers and add an account-wide 'stop' switch to block outgoing payments.

beats.what: Under the draft, any transfer above a threshold alerts the trusted person, who has one hour to approve or reject; unapproved ones are cancelled.
beats.why: RBI wants to curb digital payment fraud and give customers more control over channels and limits.
beats.care: A stop switch via branch, ATM, app, net banking or IVR would block outgoing payments, new mandates and new UPI registrations.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Digital channels would be off by default for new accounts, and new cards would start with only domestic ATM and PoS use.

cards.q: Would you name a trusted person to approve big transfers?

qs: What threshold will count as a 'large' transfer?
Who would you trust with approval rights on your account?

facts.t: New accounts would get a bank-set limit for the first *24 hours* after activation.

watch: These are draft directions; RBI will finalise them after feedback. An earlier one-hour delay on all transfers was dropped.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: RBI proposes trusted approver, stop switch to curb digital fraud

fact: RBI proposes a *one-hour* trusted-person approval for large bank transfers
twist: UPI and merchant payments are excluded, and the approver carries no financial liability.
